title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page 94 of an English typescript with handwritten formulas, apparently a translation of a Russian-style text on birational geometry or surfaces; phrases like 'at the mapping f' and 'elements over V̄' suggest this. It sits on the verso of a sheet Grothendieck reused for his 1965 notes on motivic Galois groups over F̄_p. The note on the previous page says English typescript shows through from the other side.

The mathematics, in modern terms:
- Setting: f: V → V̄ is a morphism of varieties, H is a divisor on V̄ and H̃ = f^*H. O_V[NH̃] is the sheaf of rational functions with poles bounded by NH̃.
- Basis and projection formula: y_1,…,y_M is a basis of H^0(V, O_V[NH̃]). The projection formula gives f_*(O_V[NH̃]) ≅ (f_*O_V)[NH]_{V̄}.
- Choice of N: N is chosen so that the twisted sheaf (f_*O_V)[NH] is generated by its global sections at the point P̄.
- Local expansion: take α in the local ring at P and a section y nonvanishing at P. Then ᾱȳ is a local section of the pushforward at P̄, so ᾱȳ = Σ β_ν ȳ_ν with β_ν ∈ O_{V̄,P̄}. Pulling back gives αy = Σ β_ν y_ν, hence α = Σ β_ν y_ν/y.
- Conclusion: the local ring O_{V,P} is contained in the O_{V̄,P̄}-module generated by the finitely many functions y_ν/y. This is a standard finiteness step, as in proofs that a proper quasi-finite or birational map is finite, or in Zariski's Main Theorem/Stein-factorization-type arguments, or in contraction criteria for surfaces.

This typescript has no connection to the motivic content on the neighbouring pages.
errors: The phrase 'isomorphism of ringed spaces (V, f^*O_V̄) and (V̄, O_V̄)' is imprecise as written. Presumably it means the identification of V̄ with (V̄, f_*O_V) where f_*O_V = O_V̄, for example when V̄ is normal and f is birational with connected fibres. This is a translation or wording issue rather than a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Using global sections of a sufficiently twisted pushforward sheaf to show that the local rings upstairs are finite over the local rings downstairs.
ideas.modern_name: Projection formula plus Serre's global generation; finiteness step of Zariski Main Theorem / Stein factorization
ideas.where_published: EGA III (finiteness, Stein factorization), EGA IV §8 (Zariski Main Theorem)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reused sheet of someone else's English translated typescript containing a routine finiteness argument. It is not Grothendieck's work and is unrelated to the motivic notes surrounding it.
transcription_corrections: The typescript page number is 94; the handwritten archival foliation '104' appears at the lower left corner.
The page is a standalone English typescript, likely the verso of a reused sheet; it is not part of Grothendieck's French manuscript sequence.
